course_name_original: Fundamentos De Informática (I.Mecánica / I.Tecnologías Industriales / I.Energía)
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Computer Science (Mechanical Eng. / Industrial Technologies Eng. / Energy Eng.)
prerequisites: No prior requirements are needed beyond the knowledge a student should have at this level of education and the use of a personal computer at the level of a home user.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated by means of developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of operating systems, networks and programming languages
Abstract classes. Error and exception handling
teaching_methods: Distance learning according to the UNED methodological model
Theoretical-practical approach (theory followed by exercises, problems, and practice)
Access to virtual course resources (study guide, multimedia materials, solved exercises, past exams, FAQs)

assessment_methods.method: Self-assessment test for Didactic Unit 1 (Themes 1 to 3)
Theoretical/practical in-person exam (test questions and programming problem)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must pass the mandatory practical assignment prior to the exam, pass the self-assessment test for Didactic Unit I, and achieve a minimum score of 5 on the in-person theoretical/practical exam. The final grade is a weighted sum: 90% from the exam and 10% from the practical assignment, provided both are passed individually (>= 5). The practical assignment grade is saved between ordinary (June) and extraordinary (September) calls of the same academic year, but not between academic years. The exam grade is not saved between calls or academic years.
